title: Urban Pollution
bookshelves: Category: Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, Industrial processes
summary: Urban Pollution – Environmental Challenges in Healthy Modern Cities constitutes a comprehensive resource for environmental scientists, engineers, urban planners, public health professionals, and policymakers involved in addressing pollution and sustainability issues in modern urban environments. The book covers fundamental concepts, current applications, and future perspectives on urban pollution management, presenting practical solutions to contemporary environmental challenges faced by cities globally. Fifteen chapters, written by experts from around the world, explore the causes and impacts of pollution in today’s cities, from air pollution and contaminated water to excessive noise and waste. More importantly, the book explores cutting-edge solutions, including smart air quality sensors, sustainable urban planning, community-driven initiatives, and equitable policies, which together pave the way for healthier cities. The book highlights state-of-the-art research across key areas, including air quality monitoring and atmospheric science, water sanitation and urban health, waste recycling and circular economy strategies, as well as innovative technological solutions for smart cities. Organized into four comprehensive sections, Air Quality and Atmospheric Science ; Water, Sanitation, and Urban Health ; Waste, Recycling, and Circular Economy ; and Technological Innovations for Smart Cities , this book provides a comprehensive, interdisciplinary roadmap and practical guidance for reducing pollution and building healthier, more resilient urban communities, toward achieving sustainable and healthy urban environments.
